title: Production Incident: Replica WAL Replay Lag Induced by Long Standby Queries
realWorldScenario: A data science team connects to the production read-replica and runs a heavy analytics query that scans historical data for 45 minutes. Minutes later, the replica lag increases by 35 GB, and other operational read queries on the replica return stale data.
questionStatement: Explain how queries on a physical streaming read-replica can pause WAL replay. Analyze the interaction between `hot_standby_feedback`, `max_standby_streaming_delay`, and `max_standby_archive_delay`. How do you protect replicas from analytical query disruption?

symptoms: Streaming replication replay lag grows to 35 GB
Replica serves increasingly stale data to customer-facing queries
Data science query running on standby for 45 minutes
Primary database forced to hold back WAL deletions

candidateTasks: Explain why WAL replay requires ExclusiveLock to clean dead tuples
Recommend architectural isolation: dedicated analytical replica or logical replication ETL

expectedConcepts: Recovery conflict caused by WAL replay needing to remove tuples read by standby queries
hot_standby_feedback propagating snapshot to primary to delay vacuum
Risk of primary table bloat when hot_standby_feedback is enabled
Architectural segregation: separate OLTP and OLAP read replicas
hints: What happens when WAL replay wants to delete a page version that an analytics query is reading?
If max_standby_streaming_delay expires, what happens to the analytics query?
Why can hot_standby_feedback cause bloat on the primary database?
